en: Run your own.
One command, HTTPS for the phones, and a server that holds none of your data.
The server is a small nginx container that serves the app, and nothing else.
It runs as a non-root user on a read-only filesystem, with no data volume.
Every response carries a strict content security policy, and it logs nothing by default.
To try it on your computer, run the script with up.
It builds the image and serves the app on localhost, port eighty eighty.
Only this machine can reach it.
Phones need HTTPS.
The encrypted store, the camera and offline use all need a secure page.
Set your domain, add dash dash TLS, and Caddy gets and renews the certificate for you.
Already run Traefik? Dash dash Traefik publishes no port and leaves the routing to your proxy.
Or skip the build, and pull the published image from the GitHub container registry.
Each image is scanned and tested in real browsers first.
To update, deploy a new image: installed apps show a calm line and wait for you to tap Reload.
Running it for a household? You can offer one AI key to everyone here.
Nginx adds the key on the server, forces the model, and passes the photo on.
It is off by default and rate limited; keep it behind a sign-in.
When you are done, down stops it. Your data stays in each browser.
The full guide is on the self-host page of the docs.
